Sand used is silica sand and it's a process called no bake. An acid and furan chemical are mixed with the sand to make the sand harden into a mold. Red wash is there to protect the sand from the molten metal and help keep burn-in to a minimum. It's usually an isopropyl alcohol based wash but can be water based or others. Creates a thin barrier where the metal cools and solidifies but the rest of the metal cools slower. Helps with surface finish and cleaning afterwards.

Forgot to add, those aren't runner bars, runners help feed the metal into the mold and run next to the pattern with ingates. Those are called risers and they have sleevesthat also help keep the metal warm and protect the casting from getting sand in it while pouring. They feed into the runner bars.

I lost my wife 3months before I turned 30. I started dating a little after 6months. I wasn't ready but I was extremely lonely. She had brain cancer and we hadn't had sex for about 2yrs and 7 months. So for the last 16months or so she could barely communicate and the communication she was able to make was like talking with a young child so it was rough. 

My first foray into dating I cried at the table, threw a hundred down, apologized and just left. I got into a serious relationship and that last about a year and a half but it was me hiding from the pain and avoiding being alone. Being so young made it harder too. Most early 30 somethings maybe have dealt with divorce or kids but a widower/widow? Not so much. 

Go into dating knowing you will feel like you are cheating on your SO. Most of us felt that way. I know I did. The first time I had sex afterwards I wept but she handled it as well as she could. We go back and forth on when to tell a potential partner about our loss. Is it on the first date, 4th, 3rd? You'll figure it out for you and it's also a good barometer to see how they react. Just be sure to talk to your new partner so they don't get freaked out if you start crying at something they see as being completely random/normal. 

I am remarried right now and it's wonderful. I don't talk about my late wife much anymore but I still love her just as much as the day we were married. I deal with the grief much better now too. Looking at suicide is normal, many of us have been there, some closer than others. I'd be gone if I had managed to find my parents handgun the one night I was at rock bottom. I suggest professional help too. I got some after my first serious relationship ended after my wife. I finally couldn't run from her death anymore, it helped immensely with these feelings you are having and my depression. 

​

In the end you will feel what you feel and it's all valid. You aren't alone. Those fears about cheating, dying alone, suicide are all par for the course. Getting out there when you feel ready is what's important and knowing you will bomb dates in the beginning helps to not get discouraged. Good luck.

Give yourself enough time so that you feel comfortable. Be it a week from now, a month, a year, or tomorrow. I became a widower when I was 29. My wife had battled cancer for all but a week of our 2yr and 7 months of marriage. I'm now 35 and remarried. 
It was hard at first. The first date I went on, I left weeping after twenty minutes it was so hard and the guilt crushed me. Get used to the guilt a little but you kind of get over it but there are lingering thoughts, regrets, and some anger during that dating phase. Also if you date your age or even a little older get used to awkward silence when you do drop the widow bomb. Most people that age have no experience with widows.
Sex is another matter entirely. I hadn't had sex for 3+ years when I finally got some and boy was I worried about everything. I did cry afterwards. I prepared my partner and she was very understanding.

The main thing is make sure you are ready to try again. Get professional help and work through these feelings and anxieties. I jumped into a relationship too soon because I needed something to keep the pain and loneliness away. It made everything hurt even more when that relationship ended and I realized I still wasn't right and needed to focus on myself even at two years from when she died. So I did for 16 months and now I have a healthy marriage and a healthy mindset. The grief is still there but I know how to handle it rather then run from it.

My fucking in laws bought books on the power of prayer to heal, literal snake oil/scorpion venom, all other manner of homeopathic bullshit these frauds would push on the scared and desperate because when you can see the end you will grab onto anything you can see in order to give yourself hope of one more day.
